title: 500 Skills, Zero Fine-Tuning: LinkedIn's Playbook for AI Agents — Ajay Prakash, LinkedIn
talk_summary: LinkedIn built an internal MCP server exposing code search, docs, Jira, Slack and other tools to coding agents, then added 'playbooks' — self-contained, composable instruction documents served as MCP tools — so agents can fetch task-specific tribal knowledge on demand. They scaled past MCP's ~30-40 tool limit with three meta-tools (search, get schema, execute) and closed the loop by having agents file PRs to fix outdated playbooks.

takeaways.technique: Meta-tool indirection to scale tool/skill catalogs
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of surfacing every tool and playbook to the agent, they expose only three meta-tools: search (by keyword/tags), get-schema, and execute; the agent discovers the right tool at runtime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we cannot scale it beyond 30 or 40 tools without degrading the uh context or degrading the performance of the system. So what we do is instead of uh surfacing all of these playbooks and tools through MCP we replace them with three meta tools

takeaways.technique: Playbooks as MCP-served instructions, self-contained and composable
takeaways.what_they_do: Instructions/prompts are packaged as tool-like playbooks with names and descriptions; invoking one returns the instructions as tool output. Each playbook does one task and references smaller playbooks for progressive discovery.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a playbook should be self-contained which means it should do a very specific task only ... break a big playbook into multiple smaller playbooks

takeaways.technique: Self-improving playbook flywheel via agent-filed PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: At end of a session the agent identifies outdated/missing info in the playbook it used, edits the repo, and opens a PR; merged PRs keep the knowledge base fresh.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we encourage the agents to whenever they use a particular playbook at the end of the session to identify the learnings ... update the playbooks and create a PR

takeaways.technique: Progressive context discovery to avoid compaction loss
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents read only the small playbook they need when they need it, rather than loading everything up front, which they say prevents context overload and mid-task compaction that loses information.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent only when it needs to read a smaller playbook instead of reading the entire all of the playbooks at once it can uh progressively go and read the playbooks

takeaways.technique: Central vs local playbooks scoped to repo
takeaways.what_they_do: Cross-cutting playbooks live centrally; repo-specific playbooks are checked into the repo and auto-picked only when the agent works in that repo, avoiding central-repo churn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: local playbooks where it these are the playbooks which are very specific to your code repository and you can just have them checked in with your repo

takeaways.technique: Single MCP server with central auth and telemetry
takeaways.what_they_do: One pre-installed local MCP server serves all tools and playbooks, auto-updated hourly, giving centralized auth and telemetry for learning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is one MCP server which is serving all of the uh playbooks and tools. So this man helps us do a lot of uh central things like seamless authentication, telemetry
